parole.testo: From Malay bilik / بيليق (“cabin of a junk”), from Hokkien 峇厘 (bâ-lî, “cabin of a junk”).

parole.significato: chief sailor, foreman of the seafarers, tindal, boatswain's mate
parole.testo: Borrowed from Malay tandil (“foreman, overseer”), itself from Tamil தண்டல் (taṇṭal), from Proto-Dravidian *tanḍal-. Found also in English from other Dravidian languages as tindal.

parole.significato: jong, junk (flat Southeast Asian ship with two to three masts and square bows)

parole.testo: From Malay سومڤيتن / sumpitan (“blowpipe”), derived from Malay سومڤيت / sumpit (“blowpipe”), matched to the Arabic root س ب ط (s b ṭ) “related to slenderness, lankness”. Also passed into Persian زبطانه (zabatâne), زربطانه (zarbatâne).

parole.significato: relating to the tin-exporting town قَلْعَة (qalʕa)
parole.testo: قَلْعَة (qalʕa, “a tin-exporting town on the Malacca Peninsula”) + ـِيّ (-iyy), possibly also directly from the Malay kaleng (“tin”), but this word might be etymologically identical to the place name, if it is Kelang, meaning the largest port-town in Malaysia and heavy tin-exporter now and yore and

parole.significato: kapok, silk-cotton tree (the fibre of Ceiba pentandra, less often of Bombax ceiba or trees)
